author: raman118
body:
#### References to other Issues or PRs

Fixes #24811.

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

`FpSubgroup.to_FpGroup()` omitted the required generators argument when calling `FpGroup.subgroup()`, raising `TypeError`. It now passes the generators along with the optional cached coset table, so conversion works before or after calling `order()`.

#### Other comments

The regression failed before the fix. Tests cover fresh and cached conversion, a proper subgroup, the trivial subgroup, and the whole group. Validation: `test_fp_groups.py` (8 passed, 1 slow test deselected), code-quality tests (6 passed), Ruff, and `bin/mailmap_check.py` passed.

#### AI Generation Disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) generated all changes in `sympy/combinatorics/fp_groups.py`, `sympy/combinatorics/tests/test_fp_groups.py`, and `.mailmap`. This PR description was also written by the AI agent at the account owner's request.

#### Release Notes

<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* combinatorics
  * Fixed `FpSubgroup.to_FpGroup()` raising `TypeError` when converting subgroups of finitely presented groups, with or without a cached coset table.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

+def test_fp_subgroup_to_fp_group():

linked.author: James-G-Hill
linked.body:
In the following line we can see that the method `to_FpGroup()` may return `self.parent.subgroup(C=self.C)`:

https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/75691e5cbdb3dfda4c8164a217bac6a6434404f6/sympy/combinatorics/fp_groups.py#L704

However, on `init` the internal variable `self.C` is set to `None`:

https://github.com/sympy/sympy/blob/75691e5cbdb3dfda4c8164a217bac6a6434404f6/sympy/combinatorics/fp_groups.py#L564

How should `self.C` be set? It seems to be set by the `order` method only.

I may be wrong on this and perhaps misunderstand some mathematical principle.
linked.title: `FpSubgroup.to_FpGroup()` depends on a possibly missing `self.C`?

title: Fix FpSubgroup conversion to finitely presented groups
